class: keyboard focus returning to an element a refresh detached
bounded_by: Who produces a member: the person, with ordinary input, while a scan keeps refreshing the results list. Focus leaves the row's container for a popup, another window or another control, a refresh unlinks the container it would come back to, and WPF then puts the focus somewhere else: on the list, on the window itself, or nowhere. Four ways to leave and come back are ordinary: closing or using the row's context menu, switching to another program and back (Alt+Tab, or the Explorer window Ctrl+Enter opened), a modal dialog of the app closing, and moving the focus to another control of the window and staying there. The null focus of an active window is the boundary row. How many refreshes happen in between is covered by 'refresh' being repeatable. Rows marked gap are the measured behaviour of a list that no longer refreshes (a stopped scan): the focus is not repaired there, because only a refresh repairs it; the filed follow-up that resolves the list's selected row for Ctrl+Enter flips them.

steps.focus-row: the person clicks the row 'reading-row': selected, with the keyboard focus on its container
steps.open-menu: the row's context menu opens on it, as the context-menu service opens it (placement target set, then open)
steps.close-menu: the open menu closes without a choice (Esc, or a click elsewhere)
steps.choose-menu-item: the menu's Open in Explorer entry is clicked; it must act on the row the menu was opened on
steps.deactivate: another program takes the foreground: the main window is inactive and WPF reports no focused element
steps.reactivate: the person comes back to the window
steps.modal-dialog-with-refresh: a modal dialog of the app opens, one refresh happens while it is open, and it closes
steps.focus-button: the person puts the keyboard focus on the Settings button
steps.clear-focus: nothing has the keyboard focus in an active window
steps.refresh: one tick shows a new snapshot in which 'reading-row' is a new object

expects.press-reaches-row: Ctrl+Enter executes exactly once on the current 'reading-row' object, which is selected and has the keyboard focus
expects.press-dead: Ctrl+Enter executes nothing (the measured gap of a list that no longer refreshes); the row is still selected
expects.focus-untouched-button: the Settings button still has the keyboard focus and the row is still selected
expects.menu-open-and-acts-on-row: the menu is still open with the keyboard focus inside it, no row container has the focus, and its entry acts on the row it was opened on

rows.producer: closing the row's context menu (Esc or a click elsewhere) after a refresh, then the next tick
closing the row's context menu after a refresh, on a list that no longer refreshes
choosing the menu's Open in Explorer entry after a refresh (the menu closes, the focus is handed back), then the next tick
Alt+Tab (or the Explorer window Ctrl+Enter opened) away and back, a refresh while away, then the next tick
the same, on a list that no longer refreshes
away and back with no refresh in between (control: the container is still there)
a modal dialog of the app (Settings, a confirmation) open across a refresh, closed, then the next tick
the same, on a list that no longer refreshes
a refresh while the row's context menu is open (quiet: nothing may be moved out of the menu)
the focus on another control of the window across a refresh (quiet: nothing may be moved)
boundary: an active window with nothing focused across a refresh
away across two refreshes, back, then the next tick
